title: Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa avoids club fine for angry exchange with supporters at Wolves
content:
Aston Villa have decided against fining Ezri Konsa for his frustrated exchange with supporters following Friday’s 2-0 defeat at Wolves.

Konsa, who has been standing in as captain since John McGinn’s knee injury, had to be restrained from approaching Villa’s away section by security staff after taking exception to some of the criticism aimed towards the team.

The England international had initially walked towards the away end to applaud before reacting strongly. Villa have decided against fining Konsa, but accept the defender should have not responded in that manner.

Head coach Unai Emery’s senior aides spoke to Konsa after the match to learn what had happened and while there is an understanding that it can be difficult for a player to control their reaction after a defeat, there is a feeling that the 28-year-old needed to show better composure.

“I am speaking with him to lead the team defensively, to lead with another centre back – with Tyrone (Mings), with Pau (Torres), with (Victor) Lindelof to lead the defence,” said Emery, speaking in his pre-match press conference ahead of Chelsea’s visit on Wednesday evening.

Konsa was elevated to vice captain at the start of the season and ahead of Emiliano Martinez, owing to the goalkeeper pushing for a move elsewhere last summer.

“The only problem for the club, for myself, for the players, for every worker is if we relax,” continued Emery. “If we are relaxing, we are thinking that we are everything doing fantastic. Then we are not improving because we think it’s enough. So we shouldn’t relax – keep going, keep pushing, keep improving and keep being demanding and achieve consistency through our demands. This is for Ezri and for everybody.”

Villa currently sit fourth in the Premier League, six points ahead of Chelsea, in sixth place.
